scope: Deeper follow-up on selected remaining catalogue entries. This supplements, rather than replaces, the earlier November 9 audits.
method: Read primary-paper theorem statements and formal models for changed entries, compare assumptions and objectives with the catalogue, inspect version and author metadata, and separate reported claims from independently checked arguments. Conducted additional source screening for selected unchanged entries.
limitations: This is not a complete theorem-level reassessment of all 182 problems. Earlier search-only records do not become verified by association with this audit.
Theorems and assumptions were read, but complete new proofs and Lean developments were not independently certified.
No paper's exhaustive SAT/SMT certificate corpus was replayed. The two small executable checks in tests/test_catalogue.py are editorial sanity checks, not reproductions of entire papers.
Solution-claimed labels for three-machine scheduling and moment-bounded planar FPP record manuscript claims, not accepted or referee-certified resolutions.
Some sources were inaccessible or only abstract-screened; deferred leads are listed with the relevant entry.
No git push or live deployment is part of this pass.

editorial_checks.result: K_{2,2} with red diagonal and target one has no exact matching, but its Birkhoff-face slice is the singleton all-1/2 matrix. This disproves the subsidiary identity as stated, not the main algorithmic theorem.
Enumerate all 64 orientations to check integral optimum three; half-weighted configurations provide an LP solution of value two. Minimality and uniqueness for all smaller instances are not rechecked.
